svg.title: Electron–positron annihilation
svg.desc: Top: an electron and a positron head toward each other. Bottom: after they annihilate, two photons fly off in opposite directions, carrying away their energy and momentum. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Electron–positron annihilation produces two opposite photons
Equal, opposite momenta in the center-of-momentum frame
A two-photon channel with 100 keV input kinetic energy per particle in the center-of-momentum frame.
Each photon has about 611 keV; 511 keV applies when initial kinetic energy is negligible.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
